source-8efb486855404b8e.title: SomaSmart independent marking guide
source-8efb486855404b8e.provenance: Worked answers and point-by-point guidance prepared by SomaSmart. Part maxima follow the marks printed in this paper.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Mathematics studies quantities, structures, patterns and relationships through reasoning. It includes measurements, geometry and algebra, in addition to calculations involving money.
parts.rubric: One mark for a clear definition, one for scope beyond money, and one for a suitable example.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Science uses measurement and graphs to describe experiments. Geography uses scales and coordinates to measure distances and locate places.
parts.rubric: One mark per correct subject link and one for a relevant supporting example.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: For example, budgeting, measuring ingredients, estimating travel time and comparing prices.
parts.rubric: One mark per distinct valid reason.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 3/4 and 1/5 are rational. The total is 15/20 + 4/20 = 19/20.
parts.rubric: One mark for recognising the fractions as rational, one for a common denominator and one for the total.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: √5 and π are irrational. Neither is the quotient of two integers with a nonzero denominator. √5 is the square root of a non-square integer.
parts.rubric: One mark for each named irrational number and one for the correct explanation.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: All four are real. √16 = 4, so −3 + 0 + 4.5 + 4 = 5.5.
parts.rubric: One mark for identifying all the real numbers, one for √16, one for the working and one for 5.5.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Let p be the price of a pen in TZS and n the number bought. Then 0 < p < 500 and np ≤ 2000. Four pens are affordable at any qualifying price. The largest affordable quantity is ⌊2000/p⌋ and depends on p.
parts.rubric: One mark for the strict price inequality, one for the budget relation and one for explaining the quantity or giving the four-pen guarantee. Accept an equivalent interpretation supported by working.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: No. |−7| = 7 because distance from zero is nonnegative.
parts.rubric: One mark for rejecting the claim, one for 7 and one for a valid explanation.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 5x − 10 = 15 or 5x − 10 = −15, giving x = 5 or x = −1. Both make the expression’s magnitude 15.
parts.rubric: One mark for each case set up, one for both roots and one for interpreting or checking them.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 88 km.
parts.rubric: One mark for using the tenths digit to decide and one for the rounded value.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Nearest thousand: 175,000 TZS. Nearest hundred: 175,000 TZS.
parts.rubric: Two marks per result, including a correct explanation or rounding step.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 38.2 rounds to 40 and 41.9 rounds to 40. Estimated total: 80.
parts.rubric: One mark per rounding, one for addition and one for the correct estimate.

parts.label: a
parts.rubric: Identify the first three significant digits, use the next digit and state the rounded value with units, one mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: Ignore the leading zeroes, use the third significant digit to decide and give the result with units, one mark each.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: 3.415 + 0.00879 = 3.42379, which is 3.42 to three significant figures.
parts.rubric: Two marks for the sum, one for selecting the first three significant digits and one for 3.42.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Eight ratio parts. The girls account for 5/8 × 40 = 25.
parts.rubric: One mark for eight parts, one for the girls’ share and one for 25.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: Sand is 20 × 3/2 = 30 kg.
parts.rubric: One mark for the ratio, one for substitution and one for the result with units.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: Speed is 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h. Distance in five hours is 60 × 5 = 300 km.
parts.rubric: One mark for the speed relation, one for 60 km/h, one for multiplying by five and one for 300 km.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: x + 3 fruits.
parts.rubric: One mark for each quantity and one for using addition.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark per correct expansion and one for collecting terms.

parts.label: c
parts.rubric: One each for substitution, the square, the product and the correct sum.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: 2x + 3 years.
parts.rubric: One mark for doubling x, one for adding three and one for correctly expressing the age.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark for adding five to both sides, one for dividing by three and one for the result.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: Let the number be n. Then n + 2n = 18, so 3n = 18 and n = 6.
parts.rubric: One mark each for defining the variable, forming the equation, simplifying and solving.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Let p be the price of a pencil and b the price of a pen. 2p + b = 1500 and p + 2b = 2000.
parts.rubric: One mark for the definitions and one per correct equation.

parts.label: b
parts.answer: b = 1500 − 2p. Substitute to get p + 3000 − 4p = 2000, hence p = 1000/3 and b = 2500/3.
parts.rubric: One mark for isolating b, one for substitution and one for each price.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: A pencil costs 1000/3 TZS (about 333.33 TZS). A pen costs 2500/3 TZS (about 833.33 TZS). The exact values satisfy both totals.
parts.rubric: One mark for each contextual interpretation and one for checking or explaining rounding.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: On labelled x and y axes, place A at (2, 3) and B at (4, 7).
parts.rubric: One mark for suitable axes and scale and one per correctly plotted point.

parts.label: b
parts.rubric: One mark each for the slope relation, substitution and result.

parts.label: c
parts.answer: y − 3 = 2(x − 2), so y = 2x − 1. Both points satisfy it.
parts.rubric: One mark for using the slope, one for substituting a point, one for the equation and one for a check or valid working.
